blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Local stocks fell on Wednesday as higher oil prices and a weakening peso stoked inflation concerns, while elevated treasury yields dampened demand for equities. The benchmark Philippine Stock Exchange Index (PSEi) slid 1.87 percent, or 107.64 points, to close at 5,653.55. READ: Red hot inflation seen extending BSP hikes Michael Ricafort, chief economist at Rizal Commercial Banking Corp., said the index hovered near two-week lows and its lowest level since Nov. 14, 2025. Brokerage Philstocks Financial Inc. attributed the decline to worries over the inflation outlook as investors assessed rising energy costs and the peso’s continued weakness. Philstocks said […]...
